blocks.content: The earth's crust is composed of rocks, and a rock is an aggregate of one or more minerals.

rows: Cooling and solidification of magma or lava
Deposition, compaction, and lithification of sediments
Recrystallization of pre-existing rocks under high heat & pressure
Foliated or banded structure, highly dense and hard, no fossils

items: Primary vs Derivative Rocks: Igneous rocks are primary, while Sedimentary and Metamorphic rocks are derivative.
Fossil-bearing Rocks: SSC and UPSC preliminary exams frequently ask which rock group contains fossils—the answer is Sedimentary rocks.
Metamorphic Transitions: Frequently tested parent-to-metamorphic conversions include Granite to Gneiss, Limestone to Marble, Sandstone to Quartzite, and Shale to Slate.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks form from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava and are known as primary rocks because all other rocks originate from them.
Sedimentary rocks are characterized by distinct strata (layers) and are formed through the process of lithification of broken rock fragments and organic matter.
Metamorphic rocks develop under extreme temperature (thermal) and pressure (dynamic) conditions, leading to the recrystallization and reorganization of original minerals.
Sedimentary rocks are the chief source of organic fossils and fossil fuels such as coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
The rock cycle is a continuous geological process through which old rocks are transformed into new metamorphic, igneous, or sedimentary forms.
